title: Runtime observability gap analysis + widget proposals
content:
Purpose:
This is a working gap analysis of our current inference runtime observability signals, focused on identifying missing metrics/traces and proposing new dashboard widgets (low-fidelity) we can ship in the next 2 quarters. Goal: reduce MTTI for latency regressions, make cost anomalies visible to SRE/product, and surface cache/KV inefficiencies for model teams.

Context / why this is different:
- Many existing dashboards focus on SLO-level latency and token throughput; we still lack low-cardinality, high-signal widgets for: per-model cache hit behavior, KV cache eviction shock, and short-lived end-to-end trace anchors for cold-starts across routing layers.
- This doc intentionally mixes concrete metric definition proposals (name, unit, labels, aggregation) with practical constraints (prometheus histogram bucket suggestions, cardinality limits) so implementers can start instrumenting.

Observed gaps (bulleted evidence):
- Frequent incidents where tail latency rises but service-level percentiles don’t correlate with increased host CPU/GPU — suspects: cache missstorms, routing fallback to larger models, hidden retries.
- Cost anomalies detected in billing that don't map cleanly to existing per-route token counters; we can't attribute quantization vs. model-change effects.
- Traces are too sparse around KV cache hits (we only have boolean tag on spans) and we lack a lightweight sampling strategy to capture representative cold start traces.
- Dashboard widgets overload: SLO owners want a one-glance "impact + root cause hint" tile; current boards are scattershot.

Proposal summary (high level):
1) Introduce a small set of canonical runtime metrics with strict label sets to avoid cardinality explosions.
2) Add three dashboard widgets designed for fast triage: Cache Health Heatmap, Model-Fallback Sankey (summary), and Tail Attribution Table.
3) Instrument lightweight trace anchors at 3 points: ingress router, model-exec entry, kv-cache lookup, with deterministic span ids for sampled requests.
4) Ship an alert recipe tuned for cache-miss storms and routing fallbacks (playbook included).

Detailed metric proposals (name, unit, labels, notes):
- rwi_infer_request_total (counter)
  - Unit: requests
  - Labels: service, model_id, route, region, outcome (success|retry|fallback|error)
  - Notes: coarse-grained request counter. route must be high-level (e.g., "text-gen", "embed") not endpoint path. Keep model_id as model-family only (no version) to reduce cardinality.

- rwi_token_emitted_total (counter)
  - Unit: tokens
  - Labels: service, model_family, route, origin (cache|runtime), quant_profile (low|std|hq)
  - Notes: token-level emission attribution. origin=cache means served from prefix/KV cache. quant_profile only set where available; otherwise omit.

- rwi_kvcache_hit_total / rwi_kvcache_miss_total (counters)
  - Unit: hits/misses
  - Labels: service, model_family, route, cache_shard
  - Notes: cache_shard is optional but helpful for diagnosing hot shards. Limit values to shard ids (10-50 max).

- rwi_kvcache_latency_seconds (histogram)
  - Buckets: [0.0005, 0.002, 0.01, 0.05, 0.2, 1.0]
  - Labels: service, model_family, outcome (hit|miss|error)
  - Notes: KV cache must emit this around lookup path; histogram needed to detect slow tail affecting latency. Small buckets because cache lookup is expected to be sub-ms mostly on local memory.

- rwi_model_exec_latency_seconds (histogram)
  - Buckets: [0.001, 0.005, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.5, 5.0]
  - Labels: model_family, model_variant (cpu|gpu|quant), sequence_bucket (short|medium|long)
  - Notes: sequence_bucket derived via request metadata (<=64, 65-512, >512) to avoid explosion. Avoid per-customer labels here.

- rwi_fallback_count (counter)
  - Unit: requests
  - Labels: service, model_family_from, model_family_to, reason (capacity|error|policy)
  - Notes: flux when routing falls back to different model variants — helps correlate latencies with fallback volume.

- rwi_request_retry_attempts_total (counter)
  - Unit: attempts
  - Labels: service, route, failure_mode (timeout|overload|internal)
  - Notes: surface retry storms that look like increased host load but are actually repeated ingress attempts.

Label cardinality rules (hard constraints):
- Max distinct values per label: model_family <= 50; route <= 20; region <= 8; cache_shard <= 50.
- No customer_id or request_id as a label on Prometheus metrics. Use tracing for per-request detail.
- Use coarse model_family and model_variant only.

Tracing proposals (anchors + sampling):
- Span anchors (minimal):
  1) ingress.router (span.kind=server) — attach tags: route, model_family_hint, request_size_tokens
  2) kv.cache.lookup (span.kind=internal) — attach tags: cache_key_prefix, hit(boolean), latency_ms
  3) model.exec (span.kind=client) — attach tags: model_family, variant, seq_len, kv_warm(boolean)
- Sampling strategy:
  - Deterministic 0.5% global sampling for traces (adjustable), with target enforcement to ensure: 60% of samples include at least one cache miss, 20% are long-sequence requests (>512).
  - We can implement sampling via hash(request_id) mod 200 → sample if <1 for 0.5%; then post-filter to upsample miss traces via a separate prioritized sampler that tags candidates in a lightweight span event and routes them to a high-priority trace queue.
- Trace size cap: 10 spans by default; extended traces allowed for upsampled miss/cold-start traces (max 200 spans).

Dashboard widget proposals (low-fidelity descriptions):
1) Cache Health Heatmap (compact tile)
   - Rows: model_family (top 8 by QPS), Columns: last-1h windows (15m buckets)
   - Cell value: miss_rate (rwi_kvcache_miss_total / (hit+miss))
   - Color thresholds: green <1%, amber 1–5%, red >5%
   - Purpose: immediate visibility when a model family experiences rising miss-rate across shards/regions.

2) Tail Attribution Table (wide)
   - Columns: percentile (p50,p90,p95,p99), suspected root cause (cache-miss|fallback|retry|infra), evidence links (trace id samples), route, delta vs baseline
   - Data source: Combine histogram delta queries and rwi_fallback_count, kvcache metrics.
   - Purpose: give SLO owner a single table for incident triage with suggested next step (check cache shard, evaluate fallback policy).

3) Model-Fallback Sankey (compact interactive)
   - Shows flow volume from model_family_from → model_family_to over last 1h. Width proportional to rwi_fallback_count. Hover shows reason breakdown.

4) Cold-Start Spike monitor (sparkline + count)
   - Sparkline: # cold-start traces sampled per 1m. Count: cold_start_retries_total.
   - Alert when 5m rolling average > 3x baseline.

Alerting / runbook pointers (short):
- Primary alert: rwi_kvcache_miss_rate_high
  - Trigger: any model_family with miss_rate > 3% sustained for 10m and traffic > 100 rps
  - Severity: P2
  - Playbook hints: check cache-shard memory/eviction metrics, recent config rollouts (linked to JIRA), verify upstream routing changes.

- Secondary alert: rwi_fallback_spike
  - Trigger: fallback_rate > 1% of requests and p95 model_exec_latency increased >50ms
  - Severity: P1 if user-visible SLO affected else P2
  - Playbook hints: inspect recent autoscaling events for dedicated pools, check for throttling on preferred model variants.

Implementation roadmap (milestones):
- Sprint 1 (2 weeks): add counters for kvcache hits/misses, basic token counters, and rwi_fallback_count. Implement conservative label sets.
- Sprint 2 (3 weeks): instrument kvcache_latency_histogram, model_exec_latency_histogram (sequence_bucket logic); add metric documentation and Prometheus scrape targets. Add initial Cache Health Heatmap widget (prototype).
- Sprint 3 (3 weeks): add trace anchors + prioritized sampling, hook up trace-to-metric linking (store sampled trace ids in a short-lived index for dashboard linking). Ship Tail Attribution Table and fallback Sankey.

Open questions / risks (todo items):
- Where to maintain model_family mapping (canonical source) so that dashboards don’t diverge? Suggest single source-of-truth in model-registry service with a small API returning family->alias mapping.
- KV cache visibility: some shards are managed by a separate team; how much instrumentation overhead can we impose? propose a cost budget (0.5% CPU) per shard for telemetry.
- Privacy/compliance: traced payloads must not include user PII. We must ensure span tags only contain coarse indicators and no raw request text.

Notes-to-self / quick wins:
- Add a Grafana panel that overlays kvcache_miss_rate with p99 model_exec_latency for the model_family in question — low effort, high signal.
- Spike a column in release checklist for any model rollout to include expected cache-warmup behavior and an instrumentation verification step.
- Create a short runbook snippet for oncall that maps "cache miss storm" → top 3 immediate checks to run (shard evictions, recent deployment, routing table).

Appendix: example queries (PromQL-like)
- kvcache miss rate (1h, 5m buckets):
  sum by (model_family) (increase(rwi_kvcache_miss_total[1h])) / (sum by (model_family) (increase(rwi_kvcache_hit_total[1h]) + increase(rwi_kvcache_miss_total[1h])))

- p99 model_exec_latency delta vs baseline:
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, model_family) (increase(rwi_model_exec_latency_seconds_bucket[5m]))) - baseline_p99_value (baseline stored as metric or external config)

- fallback sankey source (agg per hour):
  sum by (model_family_from, model_family_to) (increase(rwi_fallback_count[1h]))

If reviewers agree with the high-level constraints (label cardinality + sequence_bucket policy), I can spin up a small PR for Sprint 1 instrumentation and a demo dashboard for next oncall rotation.

End of working draft. Not polished — intended for feedback.
